newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Over 6,000 Sri Lankans to get Gulf compensation.
newsitem.headline: Over 6,000 Sri Lankans to get Gulf compensation.

text.p: More than 6,000 Sri Lankans will receive compensation from the U.N. Gulf War reparations body for losses incurred during the 1990 Gulf War, an official of the Bureau of Foreign Employment said on Saturday.

"Money has been credited to the bureau's account. We have instructions to give $2,500 each to 6,385 Sri Lankans who were displaced and lost income as a result of the Gulf War," Kusal Perera, the bureau's public relations manager, told Reuters.
He said the bureau would advertise the names of recipients next week and ask them to come forward to claim their money.

The U.N. Compensation Commission said this week it had paid $144 million to 63 governments for distribution to 57,636 people who had proved they were forced to leave Kuwait or Iraq or who had lost up to $100,000 in income due to the war.
It said Sri Lankan workers would receive a total of $15.9 million.
The bureau's chairman Nissanka Wijeratne earlier told Reuters about 70,000 Sri Lankans have been approved by the U.N. body as eligible to receive compensation.

A large number of individuals, corporations and governments have filed claims valued at more than $220 billion against Baghdad for losses incurred as a direct result of Iraq's invasion of Kuwait and its seven-month occupation in 1990.

The U.N. commission, funded largely by donations and seized Iraqi assets, previously paid $13.4 million in compensation to 3,966 people who had proved the death of close relatives or serious injury to themselves.
They included 34 Sri Lankans who received a total of $130,000, the bureau said.
"Many are still awaiting compensation," Perera said. "There is a possibility that about 10,000 more Sri Lankans could be paid around August."
Nearly 600,000 Sri Lankans work in the Middle East and 65 percent of them are female housemaids. Their remittances have been the top foreign exchange earner for Sri Lanka for the past five years.
